title: Add and Subtract Decimals · Part 2
note: GENERATED by scripts/generate-part-two.mjs from the core lesson — do not hand-edit.
contentObjective: I can add and subtract decimals by lining up the place values and the decimal points.
languageObjective: I can explain my steps using the words decimal, place value, tenths, hundredths, and add zeros.

vocabulary.definition: Combine or find the difference between decimals by lining up equal place values.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Combinar o hallar la diferencia entre decimales alineando valores posicionales iguales.
vocabulary.cloze: Line up equal ___ ___ before you add or subtract decimals.

examples.why: Equal place values sit in the same column.

examples.text: 12.4 + 3.75 with the last digits lined up
examples.why: Aligning the ends puts tenths under hundredths.

vocabulary.definition: A number with a dot, like 0.5, that shows a part less than one.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Un número con un punto, como 0.5, que muestra una parte menor que uno.
vocabulary.visual: 3.75 means 3 ones + 7 tenths + 5 hundredths — it is between 3 and 4
vocabulary.cloze: A number that uses a point to show a value less than one whole is a ___.

examples.why: A part less than one, written after the point.
Without the point it is five wholes.

vocabulary.definition: What a digit is worth based on where it sits in a number.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Lo que vale un dígito según el lugar que ocupa en el número.
vocabulary.visual: In 4.38: the 4 = 4 ones, the 3 = 3 tenths (0.3), the 8 = 8 hundredths (0.08)
vocabulary.cloze: The value a digit has based on its position in a number is its ___.

examples.why: Its worth comes from the column it sits in.
That reads the digit and ignores its column.

vocabulary.definition: The first spot after the decimal point. It shows parts out of 10.
vocabulary.definitionEs: El primer lugar después del punto decimal. Muestra partes de 10.
vocabulary.visual: 0.7 = 7/10 — like 7 slices of a pizza cut into 10 equal slices
vocabulary.cloze: The first place to the right of the decimal point is the ___ place.

examples.why: That 3 is in the hundredths place.

vocabulary.definition: The second spot after the decimal point. It shows parts out of 100.
vocabulary.definitionEs: El segundo lugar después del punto decimal. Muestra partes de 100.
vocabulary.visual: 0.05 = 5/100 — like 5 pennies out of a dollar (100 pennies)
vocabulary.cloze: The second place to the right of the decimal point is the ___ place.

examples.why: That 7 is in the tenths place.

vocabulary.definition: Adding zeros at the end of a decimal so numbers line up evenly.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Agregar ceros al final de un decimal para que los números se alineen.
vocabulary.visual: 15.7 becomes 15.70 so you can subtract 15.70 − 8.36 with aligned place values
vocabulary.cloze: Writing extra zeros at the end of a decimal so the places line up is called ___.

examples.why: The extra zero gives the hundredths column a digit.
That changes the value instead of padding it.

steps: 1. Line up the decimal points vertically by place value
2. Insert placeholder zeros so each number has the same number of decimal digits
3. Add or subtract right-to-left, regrouping as needed, and drop decimal straight down

revealWordProblem.title: Apply: Cargo Bay Weight Log
revealWordProblem.text: The cargo bay scale reads 342.6 kilograms of supplies. The crew unloads 128.75 kilograms of food for the mess hall, and then loads 56.4 kilograms of water samples collected during the spacewalk. What is the final cargo weight on the scale? Explain your steps.
revealWordProblem.sampleAnswer: First subtract the unloaded food: 342.60 − 128.75 = 213.85 kilograms. Then add the water samples, annexing a zero so 56.4 becomes 56.40: 213.85 + 56.40 = 270.25 kilograms. The final cargo weight is 270.25 kilograms.

reviewCheck.stem: A student buys items costing $4.59, $12.75, and $3.80. What is the total cost?
reviewCheck.explanation: 4.59 + 12.75 + 3.80 = 21.14. Line up decimal points and add column by column.
choiceFeedback: Line up the decimal points—are the place values matched?
Recheck the tenths column: 5 tenths + 7 tenths + 8 tenths. That total regroups, and something is still left behind in the tenths place.
One column got carried twice. Add each column once, and regroup only the whole tens that actually come out of that column.
hints: Three prices, all in dollars and cents — every number already has two decimal places, so the columns line up cleanly.
Stack all three amounts with the decimal points in one column, then add the cents first, carrying as you go.
Start at the hundredths: 9 + 5 + 0 = 14 — write 4 and carry 1 into the tenths column. Keep moving left one column at a time.
reviewCheck.stemEs: Un estudiante compra artículos que cuestan $4.59, $12.75 y $3.80. ¿Cuál es el costo total?
reviewCheck.explanationEs: 4.59 + 12.75 + 3.80 = 21.14. Alinea los puntos decimales y suma columna por columna.
hintsEs: Tres precios, todos en dólares y centavos: cada número ya tiene dos decimales, así que las columnas se alinean sin problema.
Acomoda las tres cantidades con los puntos decimales en una sola columna y suma primero los centavos, llevando cuando haga falta.
Empieza en las centésimas: 9 + 5 + 0 = 14 — escribe 4 y lleva 1 a las décimas. Sigue moviéndote una columna a la izquierda.
